boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Bethel University

cards.title: Royal Grounds
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Coffee and Subs
cards.notes: Located in Brushaber Commons, this spot serves Caribou Coffee and hot sub sandwiches until 10:30 p.m. on weeknights.

cards.evidence_claim: Royal Grounds is open Monday through Thursday until 10:30 p.m. and serves hot sub sandwiches and Freschetta pizzas starting after 6 p.m.

cards.title: Perkins Restaurant & Bakery
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Breakfast Hub

cards.evidence_claim: The Perkins location at 1495 County Road B West in Roseville is open 24 hours daily.
cards.source_title: Perkins at 1495 County Road B West Roseville, MN
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Raising Cane's

cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 a.m. on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: McDonald's
cards.subtitle: Midnight Snack Stop

cards.short_summary: Standard late-night fast food option located in nearby Arden Hills.

cards.source_title: Fast Food in Arden Hills, MN at 1313 W County Road E | McDonald's
cards.access_notes: Open until 12:00 a.m. daily.

cards.title: Davanni's
cards.subtitle: Local Pizza and Hoagies
cards.notes: A Twin Cities favorite for hot hoagies and pizza, located just north of the Bethel campus.
cards.short_summary: Local pizza and hoagie chain popular for group orders and casual dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arden Hills location at 3673 Lexington Ave N is a established local spot for pizza and hoagies near Bethel.
cards.access_notes: Typically open until 9:00 p.m. or 10:00 p.m.; check seasonal hours.

cards.title: 3900 Grill
cards.subtitle: Evening Grill Specials
cards.notes: Located outside the main dining center, offering grilled specials and paninis until 7:00 p.m. on weeknights.
cards.short_summary: On-campus retail dining location offering fresh grilled items and Mediterranean cuisine.
cards.evidence_claim: 3900 Grill is open Monday through Thursday until 7:00 p.m. for grilled and pressed items.
cards.access_notes: Open until 7:00 p.m. Monday-Thursday; closed weekends.

cards.title: Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Cravings
cards.notes: A go-to for late-night tacos and burritos, with drive-thru service often available past midnight.
cards.short_summary: Fast-food Mexican-inspired chain with late-night drive-thru hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Taco Bell at 2219 Highway 10 in Mounds View/Arden Hills area serves the local community with late-night options.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell® Restaurant Near Me in Saint Paul, MN
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru typically open late; check specific daily hours.

cards.title: Monson Dining Center
cards.subtitle: The Main Dining Hall
cards.notes: Known as 'The DC,' this is the primary buffet-style dining area on campus for dinner until 7:00 p.m.
cards.short_summary: Bethel's largest on-campus dining facility offering a variety of stations and community seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Monson Dining Center is open for dinner until 7:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Dinner hours end at 7:00 p.m. on weekdays and 6:30 p.m. on weekends.

cards.title: The Original Malt Shop
cards.subtitle: Classic Malts and Burgers
cards.notes: A nostalgic spot for burgers and thick malts, located south of campus in Roseville.
cards.short_summary: Classic American malt shop serving traditional burgers and ice cream treats.
cards.evidence_claim: The Original Malt Shop at 1125 Larpenteur Ave W in Roseville is a local destination for malts and burgers.
cards.access_notes: Typically open until 8:00 p.m. or 9:00 p.m.

cards.title: Snuffy's Malt Shop
cards.subtitle: Retro Diner Experience
cards.notes: A 1950s-style diner known for its burgers and malts, located in the Highland Park area of St. Paul.
cards.short_summary: Iconic Twin Cities malt shop offering a retro dining experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Snuffy's Malt Shop is a well-known local chain for burgers and malts in the St. Paul area.
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by location; check website for current status.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the specific campus spots where Bethel students actually spend their time, from the 'Egg' stairs to the quiet docks of Lake Valentine.

cards.title: The Egg Stairs
cards.subtitle: Brushaber Commons Atrium
cards.notes: Meet friends at the base of this central staircase for people-watching or to catch annual traditions like 'Christmas on the Egg.'
cards.short_summary: A central atrium staircase in the Brushaber Commons known by students as 'The Egg' for its distinctive shape and role as a social hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Students refer to the Brushaber Commons staircase as 'The Egg' and use it as a primary meeting spot and event location.
cards.access_notes: Open during Brushaber Commons building hours; accessible to all students.

cards.title: The Underground
cards.subtitle: Brushaber Commons Level 2
cards.notes: Head here for free 24/7 coffee, pool tables, and a dedicated lounge space designed specifically for commuters and PSEO students.
cards.short_summary: A renovated lower-level community space featuring games, 24/7 coffee, and resources for commuter students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Underground is a designated commuter lounge featuring free coffee 24/7 and various recreational equipment.
cards.access_notes: Located on Level 2 of BC; features 24/7 coffee access for students.

cards.title: Lake Valentine Dock
cards.subtitle: North End of Campus
cards.notes: Walk to the north end of campus to find this quiet dock, a favorite spot for sunset viewing and deep conversations away from the main buildings.
cards.short_summary: A peaceful wooden dock on the shores of Lake Valentine used by students for reflection and viewing sunsets.
cards.evidence_claim: The dock on Lake Valentine is a documented student spot for viewing sunsets and having 'deep talks.'
cards.source_title: Verdict: Lake Valentine is actually safe - The Clarion
cards.access_notes: Accessible via walking trails at the north end of campus.

cards.title: Kresge Courtyard Fire Pits
cards.subtitle: East of Brushaber Commons
cards.notes: Gather around the gas fire pits in this student-funded courtyard for late-night s'mores or outdoor study sessions.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor gathering space featuring commercial-grade gas fire pits and device charging stations.
cards.evidence_claim: Kresge Courtyard features two commercial-grade gas fire pits and was funded by the Bethel Student Government.
cards.source_title: Bethel Student Government (BSG) Funds Patio Expansion in Kresge Courtyard
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space accessible year-round; fire pits are typically available for student use in the evenings.

cards.title: The Shack
cards.subtitle: Nelson Hall Lounge
cards.notes: Visit the main lounge of Nelson Hall, known as 'The Shack,' for nightly RA-led activities and community hangouts.
cards.short_summary: The central community lounge in Nelson Hall where nightly programming and social events take place.
cards.evidence_claim: The common lounge area in Nelson Hall is called 'The Shack' and hosts nightly activities.
cards.access_notes: Primarily for Nelson Hall residents, but often hosts open events for the freshman community.

cards.title: Wellness Center Cardio Floor
cards.subtitle: WLC Level 2
cards.notes: Use the treadmills on the second floor for a workout with floor-to-ceiling views of the campus woods and Lake Valentine.
cards.short_summary: The upper level of the Wellness Center featuring extensive cardio equipment and scenic campus views.
cards.evidence_claim: The top floor of the Wellness Center is dedicated to general fitness and features 37 pieces of cardio equipment with large windows.
cards.source_title: Wellness Center - Facilities - Bethel University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Free access for students with Bethel ID; closed during chapel hours (10:10-11 a.m. MWF).

cards.title: The Loft
cards.subtitle: Near the President's Office
cards.notes: Find this quiet, sun-drenched study area located just outside the president's office for focused work between classes.
cards.short_summary: A bright and quiet study space available to all students during business hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Loft is a bright, quiet study space available to all students, located just outside the president's office.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday, 7:30 a.m.-5 p.m.

cards.title: Hagstrom Level 2 Lounge
cards.subtitle: Hagstrom Center
cards.notes: A reliable spot for a quick snack and study break, featuring vending machines and seating in the heart of the academic complex.
cards.short_summary: A functional student lounge area in the Hagstrom Center known for its convenient vending access.
cards.evidence_claim: Vending machines and student seating are located on level 2 of the Hagstrom Center.
cards.source_title: St. Paul Campus Information - Bethel University
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; accessible via skyway.

cards.title: Monson Balcony
cards.subtitle: Brushaber Commons Level 4
cards.notes: Escape the main dining hall rush by heading to the balcony level for a quieter meal with views of the atrium.
cards.short_summary: The upper seating level of the main dining center, offering a more secluded atmosphere for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Monson Dining Center includes a quieter balcony level for student seating.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Monson Dining Center operating hours; requires meal plan or door rate for entry.

cards.title: Royal Grounds Patio
cards.subtitle: Brushaber Commons
cards.notes: Grab a boba tea or Caribou Coffee and head to the adjacent seating area with large windows overlooking the campus landscape.
cards.short_summary: The seating area for the campus coffee shop, known for its views and central location.
cards.evidence_claim: Royal Grounds is the campus coffee shop serving Caribou Coffee and boba tea, located in the Brushaber Commons with views of Lake Valentine.
cards.access_notes: Open daily during the academic year; hours vary during breaks.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social activities and public spaces at Bethel University, from lakeside nature trails and disc golf to student-led worship and gallery exhibits.

cards.title: Play a Round of Disc Golf
cards.subtitle: 18-hole course near Lake Valentine
cards.notes: Challenge friends on this top-ranked 18-hole course. It is free for students and the public, featuring wooded lines and elevation changes.
cards.short_summary: A highly-ranked 18-hole disc golf course open to the public and students for free.
cards.evidence_claim: Bethel's free disc golf course offers 18 holes across campus and is open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; respect campus rules as it is private property.

cards.title: Hike the Nature Trail
cards.subtitle: Perimeter trail around Lake Valentine
cards.notes: Walk through oak savannah and wetlands on this scenic perimeter trail. It's a quiet spot for a nature break between classes.
cards.short_summary: A scenic nature trail winding through diverse ecosystems around the campus perimeter.
cards.evidence_claim: The Russell W. Johnson Nature Trail winds its way around the perimeter of the Bethel University Campus and is open for walking and running.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students and the public during daylight hours.

cards.title: Browse the Olson Gallery
cards.subtitle: Art exhibits in the Community Life Center
cards.notes: View contemporary art from national and international artists. The gallery is free and open to the public daily.
cards.short_summary: A campus art gallery featuring rotating exhibitions of professional and student work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Olson Gallery exhibits nationally and internationally established artists and is open to the public with no admission fee.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9 a.m.-7 p.m. and weekends 11 a.m.-6 p.m.

cards.title: Play Games in the Underground
cards.subtitle: Student lounge in the Brushaber Commons
cards.notes: Challenge friends to pool, ping-pong, or classic arcade games. This renovated space is a hub for student relaxation and free entertainment.
cards.short_summary: A student community space featuring free arcade games, pool tables, and board games.
cards.evidence_claim: The Underground features new arcade games, pool and pingpong tables, and board games available for student use.
cards.access_notes: Primarily for Bethel students; features 24/7 free coffee for commuters.

cards.title: Attend Sunday Night Vespers
cards.subtitle: Student-led worship service
cards.notes: Join thousands of students for this Sunday night worship tradition. It is a stripped-down, music-focused service open to the community.
cards.short_summary: A popular weekly student-led worship gathering held on Sunday evenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Every Sunday night, the Bethel community gathers for a student-led Vespers service which is free to attend.
cards.source_title: 10 Fun Things to Do on Bethel's Campus
cards.access_notes: Held Sunday nights; open to students and the public.

cards.title: Hang by the Fire Pits
cards.subtitle: Outdoor gathering space
cards.notes: Gather around the gas fire pits for s'mores or late-night study sessions. The courtyard features LED-lit bollards and charging stations.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor patio area with fire pits and seating for social gatherings and studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The fire pits in Kresge courtyard give students a reason to get outside and gather into the evening.
cards.source_title: Bethel Student Government (BSG) Funds Patio Expansion
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space accessible year-round to the campus community.

cards.title: Rent a Board Game
cards.subtitle: Free game rentals for students
cards.notes: Check out Settlers of Catan or Codenames for a free game night. The library offers a wide selection of games for checkout with a student ID.
cards.short_summary: The campus library provides free rentals of popular board and card games to students.
cards.evidence_claim: Students can rent a variety of board games from the Bethel Library at no cost.
cards.source_title: 10 Fun Things to Do on Bethel's Campus
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid Bethel student ID for checkout.

cards.title: Join a Fitness Class
cards.subtitle: Free group workouts for students
cards.notes: Attend yoga or HIIT classes without paying a membership fee. Students get free access to all cardio and strength equipment.
cards.short_summary: A 11,000 square foot fitness facility offering free classes and equipment to students.
cards.evidence_claim: Students and employees receive free access to the Wellness Center, including group fitness classes.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; closed during chapel hours (10:10-11 a.m. MWF).

cards.title: See a Student Music Recital
cards.subtitle: Free performances in the Great Hall
cards.notes: Watch talented peers perform in this world-class acoustic venue. Most student and faculty music recitals offer free admission with a student ID.
cards.short_summary: A premier performing arts venue hosting free concerts and recitals for the university community.
cards.evidence_claim: College students receive free admission to many music performances at Benson Great Hall with a valid ID.
cards.source_title: Handbell Ensemble Spring Concert | Bethel University
cards.access_notes: Free for college students with ID at the door for most departmental events.

cards.title: Study in The Loft
cards.subtitle: Quiet lounge near the President's Office
cards.notes: Find a quiet corner to focus in this bright, elevated study space. It's a dedicated 'third space' for students to work between classes.
cards.short_summary: A bright and quiet designated study space available to all students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Loft is a bright, quiet study space available to all students, located just outside the president's office.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday, 7:30 a.m.-5 p.m.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For

cards.title: Library Group Study Rooms

cards.notes: Reserve a room for up to 3 hours daily. These spaces feature large whiteboards and power outlets, ideal for collaborative projects or focused group sessions.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group study rooms equipped with whiteboards and power outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Rooms can be reserved for up to 3 hours per day; Bethel ID is required at all study room check-ins.
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; reservation required via LibCal with a Bethel email address.

cards.title: Royal Grounds Coffee Shop
cards.subtitle: Brushaber Commons, Level 2

cards.evidence_claim: Royal Grounds is open for most of the day, making it the perfect place to take a study break.

cards.title: Dining Center Balcony

cards.access_notes: Accessible during dining center operating hours; typically requires a meal plan or purchase for entry during meal times.

cards.evidence_claim: In the open community spaces are clusters of soft seating, flexible work stations, and charging stands.
cards.source_title: A New Home for Bethel Seminary
cards.access_notes: Open to students; features free Wi-Fi and plentiful parking.

cards.title: RC Third Level Seating
cards.subtitle: Robertson Center, Level 3
cards.notes: This updated corridor features new seating and lighting, providing a convenient spot for quick study sessions between classes in the RC and HC.
cards.short_summary: A recently renovated corridor with dedicated seating for students between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: The third level corridor of the RC has been updated with new paint, carpet, ceiling, lighting, and seating.
cards.source_title: Summer Construction Brings a Fresh Look to Bethel Drive
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during academic building hours.

cards.title: Nelson Hall Study Area
cards.subtitle: Nelson Hall, Level 1
cards.notes: A renovated space for freshman residents featuring soft seating and a dedicated study area that opens into a large community lounge with a fireplace.
cards.short_summary: A modern community lounge and study area within Bethel's largest freshman residence hall.
cards.evidence_claim: A brand new shack and study area also open into the lounge space, making it feel much larger.
cards.source_title: Summer Construction Brings Renewal to Favorite Spaces
cards.access_notes: Primarily for residents of Nelson Hall; accessible via student ID.

cards.title: Library Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Hagstrom Center, Level 3
cards.notes: Available for independent use, this space supports creative projects and non-traditional study with staff and student advisors available for help.
cards.short_summary: A creative space within the library for independent project work and collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Makerspace is available for independent use during library hours.
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; check for specific advisor availability.

cards.title: Individual Study Carrels

cards.notes: Find a quiet corner among the book stacks. These individual carrels are perfect for deep focus and long-form writing without distractions.
cards.short_summary: Quiet individual study desks located within the library's book stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: The building consists of book stacks and various individual study carrels and lounge area.
cards.access_notes: Available on a first-come, first-served basis during library hours.

cards.title: Wellness Center Lounge
cards.subtitle: Wellness Center, Level 2
cards.notes: Located between the RC and HC, this area offers a bright environment for students to work before or after a workout session.
cards.short_summary: A bright lounge area within the Wellness Center for student use.
cards.evidence_claim: Stop by the Wellness Center at WLC200 on the second level between the Hagstrom Center (HC) and Robertson Center (RC).
cards.access_notes: Open during Wellness Center hours; closed for Chapel on MWF 10:10-11 a.m.

cards.title: Niche Departmental Lounges
cards.subtitle: Various Academic Buildings
cards.notes: Over half of Bethel's 18 departments have dedicated lounges. These spaces offer a unique environment to study in proximity to professors and peers.
cards.short_summary: Specialized study and social spaces maintained by individual academic departments.
cards.evidence_claim: Out of the 18 departments on campus, more than half have a space of their own to provide homework space.
cards.source_title: Bethel's not-so-secret student spaces - The Clarion
cards.access_notes: Access varies; some are open to all, while others require major-specific keypad codes.

cards.evidence_claim: Snelling Avenue runs through Arden Hills offering a convenient route for businesses and residents near Bethel University.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique spiritual and community-driven traditions that define the Royal experience at Bethel University in Minnesota.

cards.title: Vespers Sunday Night Worship
cards.subtitle: A student-led musical worship tradition since the 1980s
cards.notes: Gather at Benson Great Hall every Sunday at 9 p.m. for an hour of student-led music and prayer. It is a cornerstone of spiritual life on campus.
cards.short_summary: A weekly, student-led musical worship service that has been a staple of Bethel spiritual life for over 30 years.
cards.evidence_claim: Vespers is a weekly musical worship service formed by students in the 1980s, held every Sunday night at 9 p.m. in Benson Great Hall.
cards.source_title: What Does Vespers Mean to Bethel Students?
cards.access_notes: Open to students, alumni, and the community; held Sunday nights during the academic semester.

cards.title: Broomball Under the Lights
cards.subtitle: The signature winter intramural sport
cards.notes: Join a team in January to play this hockey-like sport using brooms and a ball on the campus ice rinks. It is a decades-old winter tradition.
cards.short_summary: A beloved winter tradition where students compete in intramural broomball leagues on campus ice rinks during the cold Minnesota months.
cards.evidence_claim: Broomball is a favorite Bethel tradition involving winter leagues and an alumni tournament, described as a 'beginning of life-long devotion' for many.
cards.access_notes: Games typically occur in the evenings from January through February.

cards.title: Festival of Christmas
cards.subtitle: A 70-year musical celebration of Advent
cards.notes: Attend this massive multi-choir and orchestral performance in Benson Great Hall, featuring a candlelight processional and sacred music.
cards.short_summary: An annual Christmas performance featuring over 300 student musicians, a tradition that has run for 70 years.
cards.evidence_claim: The Festival of Christmas is in its 70th year as of 2026, featuring a candlelight processional and performances by various Bethel choirs and ensembles.
cards.access_notes: Requires tickets; usually held the first weekend of December.

cards.title: The High-Energy Move-In
cards.subtitle: Upperclassmen 'herds' greeting new students
cards.notes: Watch as energetic student volunteers dance and haul luggage to dorm rooms to welcome the incoming class. It is a signature high-energy start.
cards.short_summary: A decades-old tradition where upperclassmen volunteers energetically assist new students with moving into their residence halls.
cards.evidence_claim: Welcome Week move-in involves 'herds of caffeinated upperclass student volunteers dancing energetically as they unpack new students' cars.'
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually in late August during the first days of Welcome Week.

cards.title: Finals Week Midnight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Late-night fuel before exams
cards.notes: Head to the Dining Center at 11:45 p.m. during finals week for a late-night meal served by faculty and staff to celebrate the semester's end.
cards.short_summary: A finals week tradition where students gather for a late-night breakfast served by university staff to relieve exam stress.
cards.evidence_claim: Midnight Breakfast is a finals week tradition held from 11:45 p.m. to 12:30 a.m. in the dining commons.
cards.access_notes: Held late at night (11:45 PM) during finals week in the Monson Dining Center.

cards.title: Core Group Family Units
cards.subtitle: Small group bonding for new students
cards.notes: Join your assigned 'family unit' of 15 students led by upperclassmen to navigate your first week and build immediate community connections.
cards.short_summary: Small orientation groups, known as Core Groups, that serve as a primary social unit for new students during Welcome Week.
cards.evidence_claim: Core Groups are described as a 'Welcome Week family unit' including about 15 other students led by upper-class students.
cards.access_notes: Specific to new students during orientation week.

cards.title: Last Day Cookie Tent
cards.subtitle: Fresh cookies and cocoa on the patio
cards.notes: Visit the Brushaber Commons patio on the last day of fall classes for free freshly baked cookies and hot cocoa, often featuring a visit from Santa.
cards.short_summary: An annual event on the last day of classes where the dining service provides free cookies and treats to students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sodexo Cookie Tent is an annual event on the last day of classes featuring freshly baked cookies and hot cocoa on the BC Patio.
cards.access_notes: Typically held from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. on the final day of fall semester classes.

cards.title: Spring Fling Mocktails
cards.subtitle: End-of-year outdoor celebration
cards.notes: Celebrate the end of the spring semester with mocktails, frozen yogurt, and photo booths at the CLC Circle. Arrive early for free treats.
cards.short_summary: A year-end social event for students featuring outdoor activities, non-alcoholic drinks, and community bonding.
cards.evidence_claim: Spring Fling features mocktails, frozen yogurt, and a photobooth at the CLC Circle, sponsored by Bethel Student Government.
cards.access_notes: Held in May; rain plan moves the event inside Brushaber Commons.

cards.title: The Wildcat Bonfire
cards.subtitle: Igniting school spirit behind the stadium
cards.notes: Gather behind the stadium during Homecoming weekend for a massive bonfire to rally support for the Royals. It is a classic fall spirit event.
cards.short_summary: A traditional bonfire held during Homecoming weekend to build community and school spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wildcat Bonfire is a scheduled event during Homecoming, typically held behind the stadium.
cards.access_notes: Open to students and alumni during Homecoming weekend, usually in October.

cards.title: Vespers Under the Lights
cards.subtitle: Outdoor worship at Royal Stadium
cards.notes: Experience a special outdoor edition of the Vespers service held under the stadium lights to kick off the fall semester. It is a new campus tradition.
cards.short_summary: A recently established tradition of holding the first Vespers service of the fall semester outdoors at the football stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: The first Vespers service of the fall semester is now held under the new lights at Royal Stadium, marking a 'fresh space to gather.'
cards.source_title: Vespers under the lights: a fresh space to gather and grow
cards.access_notes: Held annually in September at Royal Stadium.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Bethel University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Arrive for Move-In Day
cards.subtitle: The start of Welcome Week
cards.notes: Enter via the west entrance where student teams help haul gear to your room. Check in at the Brushaber Commons Atrium to get your ID card and orientation materials.
cards.short_summary: Kick off your college experience with a high-energy move-in process supported by student leaders.
cards.evidence_claim: New student move-in involves entering via the west entrance with student teams assisting, followed by check-in at the Brushaber Commons Atrium.
cards.access_notes: Specific move-in time slots are assigned to students; check-in typically runs from 8:15 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.

cards.title: First Meal at Monson
cards.subtitle: Brushaber Commons Level 3
cards.notes: Swipe your new ID to enjoy a buffet-style lunch. It is a central hub for meeting floor mates and fueling up between orientation sessions.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus dining hall offering a variety of stations and community seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Monson Dining Center is located on Level 3 of Brushaber Commons and serves as the main dining location for students on meal plans.
cards.access_notes: Open daily during academic terms; students use meal plan swipes for entry.

cards.title: Welcome Kickoff Celebration
cards.subtitle: Official University Welcome
cards.notes: Gather with the entire incoming class for the official kickoff. This high-energy event marks the transition from family time to student life.
cards.short_summary: A large-scale assembly in the university's premier performing arts venue to welcome new Royals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kickoff Celebration is the official welcome for students and the final farewell for families, held in Benson Great Hall.
cards.access_notes: Typically held on the first evening of Welcome Week; arrive 15 minutes early for seating.

cards.title: Late Night Glo Party
cards.subtitle: Brushaber Commons Level 2
cards.notes: Head to the Underground for a late-night social event with music and dancing. It is a staple of the first weekend for meeting new people.
cards.short_summary: A high-energy social gathering featuring music and neon themes to help students connect.
cards.evidence_claim: The Glo Party is a scheduled late-night event during Welcome Week, often held in The Underground or similar campus spaces.
cards.access_notes: Usually starts around 9:30 p.m. during orientation weekend.

cards.title: Morning Coffee at Royal Grounds
cards.subtitle: The Campus Living Room
cards.notes: Grab a Caribou Coffee or a Bruegger's Bagel. This is the go-to spot for a quick breakfast or a casual meeting with your new roommate.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus coffee shop serving Caribou Coffee and snacks in a central social space.
cards.evidence_claim: Royal Grounds is located in Brushaber Commons and serves Caribou Coffee and Bruegger's Bagels.
cards.access_notes: Open from 7:30 a.m. on weekdays; weekend hours vary during special events.

cards.title: Walk the Nature Trail
cards.subtitle: Scenic Lake Valentine Loop
cards.notes: Take a break from sessions to walk the one-mile loop around Lake Valentine. It is a peaceful way to explore the wooded perimeter of campus.
cards.short_summary: A one-mile nature trail circling the campus and offering views of Lake Valentine.
cards.evidence_claim: The Russell W. Johnson Nature Trail is a one-mile loop that circles the campus and passes by Lake Valentine.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk for walking and running.

cards.title: Play a Round of Disc Golf
cards.subtitle: Top-Ranked Campus Course
cards.notes: Challenge your new friends to a round on this 18-hole course. It winds through the woods and is free for students to use anytime.
cards.short_summary: A highly-rated 18-hole disc golf course located on the north side of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Bethel's 18-hole disc golf course is ranked among the top college courses and is free for student use.
cards.source_title: 10 Fun Things to Do on Bethel's Campus
cards.access_notes: Course begins near Chalberg Hall; open during daylight hours.

cards.title: Kresge Kickoff
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Community Festival
cards.notes: Enjoy live music, inflatable games, and carnival food in the courtyard. This Friday night event is the first major social of the semester.
cards.short_summary: An annual outdoor festival hosted by Student Government to celebrate the start of the year.
cards.evidence_claim: Kresge Kickoff is a Friday night event featuring music, food, and games in the Kresge Courtyard.
cards.access_notes: Typically held from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. on the first Friday of the term.

cards.title: Vespers Under the Lights
cards.subtitle: Sunday Night Worship
cards.notes: Join a student-led worship service at the stadium. It is a signature tradition for grounding yourself before the first week of classes begins.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing Sunday evening worship tradition, now often held outdoors at the stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: Vespers is a student-led Sunday evening worship service that has recently been held under the lights at Royal Stadium.
cards.source_title: Vespers under the lights | Bethel University
cards.access_notes: Held Sunday evenings; check campus schedules for specific start times.

cards.title: Pick Up Your Textbooks
cards.subtitle: Brushaber Commons Level 2
cards.notes: Finalize your weekend by grabbing your books before Monday. You can also pick up some Royal blue gear to show your school spirit.
cards.short_summary: The official university bookstore for textbooks, apparel, and supplies.
cards.evidence_claim: The Campus Store is located on Level 2 of Brushaber Commons and is the primary location for textbook pickup.
cards.access_notes: Open during Welcome Week with extended hours for textbook pickup.
